name: Ulnar Artery Forearm Flap (UAFF)

dominant_pedicle.veins: Paired ulnar venae comitantes + basilic vein

perforators.label: Ulnar Septocutaneous Perforators
perforators.location: Line from medial epicondyle to pisiform between FCU and FDS
perforators.relation_to_landmarks: Distal constant perforator ~3–5 cm proximal to pisiform

vascular_anatomy.venous_drainage_notes: Dual deep venae comitantes and superficial basilic system provide reliable outflow.
vascular_variants: Ulnar artery is often dominant supply to superficial palmar arch — mandatory Allen test before sacrificing trunk

motor: Ulnar nerve lies immediately ulnar to artery in distal two-thirds — meticulous protection
nerves.donor_numbness_note: Volar-ulnar forearm numbness; protect dorsal cutaneous branch of ulnar nerve.

dimensions.thickness_notes: Thinner and less hair-bearing than radial forearm skin, with concealed ulnar donor site.

arc_of_rotation.pivot_point: Distal ulnar wrist (reverse) or cubital fossa (antegrade)
arc_of_rotation.reach_description: Free flap for oral cavity/pharynx/hand; reverse pedicled to palm and dorsum of hand.

indications: Oral cavity and pharyngeal reconstruction requiring thin hairless skin
Hand/wrist coverage
Alternative to RFFF when radial artery is unusable
contraindications: Prior ulnar nerve or vascular trauma
advantages: Less hair-bearing than RFFF
Donor bed over FDS/FCU muscle bellies takes STSG better than exposed FCR tendon
Concealed ulnar scar
disadvantages: Sacrifices dominant palmar arch artery in many patients

donor_site.closure: Primary if ≤4–5 cm; STSG over muscle bellies heals reliably.
donor_site.functional_loss: Minimal when Allen test passes and ulnar nerve is spared.

technique.patient_positioning: Supine with arm on hand table under tourniquet.
preoperative_planning: Perform modified Allen test + Doppler to confirm radial palmar arch perfusion
Map perforators along medial epicondyle–pisiform line
technique.design: Center paddle over septum between FCU and FDS in middle-to-distal volar-ulnar forearm.
harvest_steps: 1. Incise radial margin subfascially over FDS to septum between FDS and FCU.
2. Identify ulnar artery, venae comitantes, and ulnar nerve; carefully separate ulnar nerve out of flap.
3. Preserve dorsal cutaneous branch of ulnar nerve ~5 cm proximal to pisiform.
4. Release tourniquet and confirm brisk hand perfusion via radial artery before dividing ulnar pedicle.
pearls: Always perform an intraoperative vascular clamp test on the ulnar artery with tourniquet deflated before ligating it.
pitfalls: Traction or thermal injury to the ulnar nerve or its dorsal sensory branch.

references.book: Wei FC, Mardini S. Flaps and Reconstructive Surgery

name: Cross-Finger Flap (Standard & Reverse)
tissue_components: Dorsal middle phalangeal skin & subcutaneous tissue (or de-epithelialized subcutaneous flap for dorsal defects)

dominant_pedicle.artery: Random subdermal plexus from dorsal branches of proper digital artery

vascular_anatomy.venous_drainage_notes: Wide lateral hinge along mid-axial line provides robust random perfusion.
vascular_variants: Reverse turn-over de-epithelialized cross-finger flap covers dorsal defects of adjacent finger + FTSG

sensory: Dorsal digital sensory branches (optional innervated cross-finger variant)

dimensions.thickness_notes: Thin, pliable, dependable tissue matching volar pulp or middle phalanx defects with exposed tendon/bone.

arc_of_rotation.pivot_point: Mid-axial hinge on adjacent donor finger
arc_of_rotation.reach_description: Covers volar pulp/middle phalanx defects of adjacent finger (or thumb from index dorsal proximal phalanx).

indications: Volar fingertip/pulp defects with exposed bone or flexor tendon too large for V-Y advancement
Dorsal digital tendon/joint exposure (reverse cross-finger)
Thumb volar pulp defects
contraindications: Severe osteoarthritis or Dupuytren contracture with high PIP stiffness risk
Vascular compromise of adjacent donor finger
advantages: Reliable, technically straightforward workhorse in hand trauma
Preserves injured digit length
disadvantages: PIP joint stiffness risk without early therapy

donor_site.closure: Full-thickness skin graft over intact extensor paratenon.
donor_site.functional_loss: Minimal with prompt hand therapy after division.

technique.patient_positioning: Supine with hand table and tourniquet.
preoperative_planning: Preserve extensor paratenon meticulously on donor finger so FTSG takes reliably
technique.design: Rectangular flap spanning dorsal aesthetic subunit of adjacent middle phalanx, hinged toward recipient finger.
harvest_steps: 1. Incise 3 sides down to — but NOT through — extensor paratenon.
2. Elevate off paratenon carefully; divide Cleland ligaments at hinge to increase reach.
3. Open flap like a book page onto recipient finger volar defect and inset loosely.
4. Cover donor bed with FTSG + bolster; divide pedicle at 14–21 days and mobilize aggressively.
pearls: Harvesting the entire dorsal aesthetic subunit from mid-axial to mid-axial line hides the FTSG borders cleanly.
pitfalls: Stripping extensor paratenon causes donor FTSG failure and exposed extensor tendon.

recipient_vessels_options: Staged regional digital flap (division at 2–3 weeks)

name: Moberg Volar Advancement Flap

dominant_pedicle.artery: Bilateral radial and ulnar proper palmar digital arteries of thumb

minor_pedicles: Independent dorsal thumb arteries (make Moberg safe in thumb ONLY)
vascular_anatomy.venous_drainage_notes: Independent dorsal blood supply in the thumb prevents dorsal skin necrosis when volar bundles are advanced.
vascular_variants: Do NOT perform classic Moberg in index–small fingers due to risk of dorsal digital necrosis

sensory: Bilateral radial and ulnar digital nerves of thumb (intact)
nerves.donor_numbness_note: Preserves normal 2-point discrimination at thumb tip.

dimensions.thickness_notes: Glabrous, durable, sensate thumb pulp skin — ideal tactile match for pinch.

arc_of_rotation.pivot_point: Linear distal advancement (≤1.5–2.0 cm with IP flexion or O'Brien proximal release)
arc_of_rotation.reach_description: Covers transverse or volar-oblique thumb tip pulp defects ≤1.5–2.0 cm.

indications: Thumb tip / volar pulp amputations ≤1.5–2.0 cm with exposed distal phalanx
Sensate thumb length preservation
contraindications: Defects >2.0 cm (use FDMA kite or Littler flap)
advantages: Single-stage glabrous sensate pulp with normal 2-point discrimination
Preserves thumb length and pinch
disadvantages: Risk of thumb IP joint flexion contracture if advanced >1.5 cm without O'Brien release

donor_site.closure: Primary closure along mid-axial lines (or proximal FTSG / V-Y in O'Brien modification).
morbidity: IP joint flexion contracture if over-flexed

technique.patient_positioning: Supine with hand table and tourniquet.
preoperative_planning: Plan O'Brien proximal transverse incision + FTSG if >1.5 cm advancement needed
technique.design: Bilateral mid-axial incisions strictly dorsal to both neurovascular bundles extending to MP crease.
harvest_steps: 1. Make bilateral mid-axial incisions dorsal to radial and ulnar digital neurovascular bundles.
2. Elevate volar skin + both neurovascular bundles off intact FPL tendon sheath.
3. Advance distally with gentle IP flexion (≤30°); add O'Brien proximal release + FTSG if tight.
4. Inset over distal phalanx and excise small proximal Burow triangles if needed.
pearls: If thumb IP flexion exceeds 30° to reach the tip, convert to the O'Brien modification to prevent IP contracture.
pitfalls: Applying classic Moberg to non-thumb digits risks dorsal skin necrosis.

name: Atasoy–Kleinert Volar V-Y Advancement Flap

dominant_pedicle.artery: Terminal digital pulp arterial arborizations within deep subcutaneous pedicle

vascular_anatomy.venous_drainage_notes: Preserving deep subcutaneous pulp tissue while dividing only vertical fibrous septa maintains reliable viability.
vascular_variants: Contraindicated in volar-oblique loss with insufficient proximal volar pulp

nerves.donor_numbness_note: Maintains near-normal fingertip sensibility and glabrous durability.

dimensions.thickness_notes: Glabrous, padded fingertip pulp ideally matching amputated fingertip.

arc_of_rotation.reach_description: Covers transverse or dorsal-oblique fingertip amputations with exposed distal phalanx up to ~1.0 cm.

indications: Transverse fingertip amputations with exposed bone
Dorsal-oblique fingertip amputations (ideal geometry)
Nail bed support and finger length preservation
advantages: Single-stage local anesthetic procedure
Restores sensate, padded, glabrous fingertip skin
Avoids adjacent digit morbidity
disadvantages: Tip necrosis if closed under excessive tension

donor_site.closure: V-to-Y primary closure distal to DIP flexion crease.

technique.patient_positioning: Supine with digital block and finger tourniquet.
preoperative_planning: Confirm transverse or dorsal-oblique amputation angle
Do NOT extend apex of V proximal to DIP crease
technique.design: Isosceles triangle on volar pulp with base at amputation edge and apex at DIP crease.
harvest_steps: 1. Incise dermal margins carefully without cutting deep subcutaneous neurovascular pedicle.
2. Release deep vertical fibrous septa off distal phalanx periosteum and FDP sheath with tenotomy scissors.
3. Advance triangular island distally up to 1 cm and suture leading edge to nail bed.
4. Close proximal stem loosely as a Y without strangulating the subcutaneous pedicle.
pearls: Divide ONLY vertical fibrous septa—never undermine deeply through the subcutaneous fat pedicle.
pitfalls: Attempting Atasoy V-Y on a volar-oblique amputation leaves insufficient volar skin.

references.book: Atasoy E et al. J Bone Joint Surg Am (Triangular Volar Flap)

name: Littler Heterodigital Neurovascular Island Flap
region: Upper Extremity (ulnar ring / radial middle finger pulp)

dominant_pedicle.artery: Ulnar proper digital artery of middle or ring finger
dominant_pedicle.artery_origin: Common palmar digital artery (superficial palmar arch)
dominant_pedicle.veins: Perivascular venae comitantes within fibrofatty cuff

vascular_anatomy.venous_drainage_notes: ALWAYS preserve a 3–5 mm fibrofatty perivascular cuff for venous outflow.
vascular_variants: Ligate adjacent finger's proper digital artery at bifurcation to gain palmar pivot reach

sensory: Proper palmar digital nerve (consider end-to-end neurorrhaphy to thumb digital nerve to avoid cortical mislocalization)
nerves.donor_numbness_note: Donor hemi-pulp numbness; cortical mislocalization occurs unless coapted to thumb nerve.

dimensions.thickness_notes: Durable, glabrous, highly sensate pinch-surface pulp matching thumb pad.

arc_of_rotation.reach_description: Reaches entire volar thumb pulp via subcutaneous palmar tunnel.

indications: Large volar thumb pulp defects (>2 cm) requiring sensate glabrous skin
Thumb tactile restoration after avulsion or burn
contraindications: Compromised radial digital artery on donor finger
Elderly patients intolerant of cortical mislocalization
advantages: Single-stage glabrous sensate pulp for large thumb defects
Immediate robust vascularity
disadvantages: Cortical mislocalization unless nerve is coapted to thumb digital nerve

donor_site.closure: Full-thickness skin graft on ulnar aspect of donor ring/middle finger.
donor_site.functional_loss: Minimal when non-pinch ulnar border is chosen.

technique.patient_positioning: Supine on hand table under tourniquet and loupes.
preoperative_planning: Verify bilateral digital arteries in donor digit (digital Allen test)
Select ulnar border of ring or middle finger
technique.design: Template thumb pulp defect onto ulnar pulp of ring or middle finger.
harvest_steps: 1. Elevate pulp island preserving generous perivascular fibrofatty cuff around digital artery and nerve.
2. Trace pedicle into mid-palm via Brunner zig-zag; ligate adjacent finger's arterial branch at bifurcation.
3. Split common digital nerve intraneurally proximally (or divide and coapt to thumb ulnar digital nerve).
4. Pass island loosely through wide palmar tunnel to thumb pulp and graft donor finger.
pearls: Leaving a generous fatty cuff around the digital neurovascular bundle prevents postoperative venous congestion.
pitfalls: Kinking or compressing the pedicle inside a tight subcutaneous palmar tunnel.

name: Free Medial Femoral Condyle (MFC) Corticoperiosteal Flap

minor_pedicles: Superomedial genicular artery (SMGA — primary fallback in ~10–15% when DGA is absent)

perforators.label: Saphenous Artery Cutaneous Perforator
perforators.location: Distal medial thigh anterior to sartorius
perforators.relation_to_landmarks: Arises from DGA trunk allowing a monitoring/resurfacing skin paddle

vascular_anatomy.venous_drainage_notes: Paired venae comitantes join superficial femoral vein; SMGA backup has shorter pedicle (3–4 cm).
vascular_variants: DGA absent or hypoplastic in ~10–15% — harvest on SMGA instead

sensory: Saphenous nerve & infrapatellar branch (preserve to avoid neuroma)

dimensions.thickness_notes: Malleable thin corticoperiosteal graft (typically 1.5 × 2 cm up to 3 × 5 cm) ideal for small recalcitrant nonunions (<3–4 cm).

arc_of_rotation.reach_description: Gold standard vascularized small bone graft for scaphoid AVN/nonunion, lunate (MFT), talus, clavicle, and facial bone.

indications: Recalcitrant scaphoid nonunion with proximal pole AVN
Kienböck disease / lunate reconstruction (MFT osteochondral)
Small recalcitrant nonunions of clavicle, humerus, talus (<4 cm)
Nasal/maxillary/orbital bone reconstruction
contraindications: Large segmental bone defects >5–6 cm (use free fibula)
advantages: Minimal knee donor morbidity and rapid ambulation
Highly osteogenic malleable vascularized bone/periosteum
Optional cartilage (MFT) or saphenous skin paddle
disadvantages: Not suitable for long load-bearing diaphyseal gaps
DGA absent in ~10–15% requiring shorter SMGA pedicle
Rare distal femoral stress fracture if oversized

technique.patient_positioning: Supine with ipsilateral knee slightly flexed and externally rotated.
preoperative_planning: Review recipient bone defect size (<4 cm ideal)
Prepare radial artery at anatomic snuffbox for scaphoid cases
technique.design: Medial distal thigh incision retracting vastus medialis anteriorly to expose condylar periosteal plexus.
harvest_steps: 1. Incise along posterior border of vastus medialis and retract anteriorly off medial intermuscular septum.
2. Visualize osteoarticular DGA branch and transverse SMGA branch directly on periosteum of MFC.
3. Protect MCL posteriorly and joint capsule distally; outline required corticoperiosteal block.
4. Trace DGA proximally to superficial femoral vessels for 6–10 cm pedicle length.
pearls: Identify both DGA and SMGA on the periosteum before making bony cuts so you can seamlessly switch to SMGA if DGA is hypoplastic.
pitfalls: Violating the MCL or harvesting an oversized structural block risking distal femur fracture.

references.book: Wei FC, Mardini S. Flaps and Reconstructive Surgery

name: Free Great Toe / Second Toe-to-Hand Transfer

dominant_pedicle.artery: First dorsal metatarsal artery (FDMA — Gilbert Types I–III) or 1st plantar metatarsal artery
dominant_pedicle.artery_origin: Dorsalis pedis artery / deep plantar arch
dominant_pedicle.veins: Dorsal venous arch / greater saphenous vein

vascular_anatomy.venous_drainage_notes: Large dorsal subcutaneous veins draining into greater saphenous system provide reliable outflow.
vascular_variants: Gilbert Type I (~45% dorsal), Type II (~35% intramuscular), Type III (~20% plantar dominant)

motor: Extrinsic hand flexor/extensor tendons repaired to toe tendons
nerves.donor_numbness_note: Preserve 1st metatarsal head to maintain normal push-off gait.

dimensions.thickness_notes: Only true functional like-for-like composite digit reconstruction providing bone, nail, glabrous pulp, sensibility, and motion.

arc_of_rotation.reach_description: Reconstructs amputated thumb (trimmed great toe / wrap-around) or fingers (2nd toe).

indications: Traumatic thumb amputation at or proximal to IP joint
Multiple finger amputations ('metacarpal hand')
Congenital symbrachydactyly / thumb aplasia
advantages: Restores opposable, sensate, mobile thumb/digit with nail and glabrous pinch
Preserves daily walking gait when 1st metatarsal head is intact

donor_site.closure: Primary closure preserving 1st metatarsal head (great toe) or wedge closure of 2nd ray.
donor_site.functional_loss: Minimal for daily ambulation when 1st metatarsal head is preserved.

technique.patient_positioning: Supine (simultaneous hand and foot teams under tourniquet).
preoperative_planning: Map dorsalis pedis & FDMA with Doppler/CTA
Choose trimmed great toe vs wrap-around vs 2nd toe
technique.design: Retrograde dissection starting in 1st web space to identify dominant dorsal vs plantar arterial system early.
harvest_steps: 1. Dissect 1st web space FIRST in retrograde fashion to determine Gilbert Type.
2. Preserve dorsal venous arch to greater saphenous vein, tendons, and plantar digital nerves.
3. Disarticulate distal to 1st metatarsal head (preserving tripod weight-bearing).
4. Fix bone, repair extensor & flexor tendons, perform vascular anastomoses, and coapt digital nerves.
pearls: Always start in the first web space (retrograde approach) so Gilbert Type III plantar-dominant anatomy is recognized immediately.
pitfalls: Resecting the 1st metatarsal head causes chronic metatarsalgia and gait disturbance.

references.book: Wei FC, Mardini S. Flaps and Reconstructive Surgery

name: Tensor Fascia Lata (TFL) Flap

perforators.label: TFL Perforator
perforators.location: 8–10 cm inferior to ASIS along anterior margin of TFL
perforators.relation_to_landmarks: Pedicle enters deep medial surface of TFL ~8–10 cm below ASIS

vascular_anatomy.venous_drainage_notes: Distal third over lower thigh is random-pattern and prone to necrosis if extended within 8 cm of lateral knee.
vascular_variants: Immediate intraoperative bailout when ALT descending branch perforators are absent

sensory: LFCN & lateral cutaneous branch of T12 (allows sensate trochanteric coverage)

dimensions.thickness_notes: Provides strong autologous vascularized fascial sheet (iliotibial band) for full-thickness abdominal wall reconstruction.

arc_of_rotation.pivot_point: Pedicle entry 8–10 cm inferior to ASIS
arc_of_rotation.reach_description: Gold standard pedicled flap for trochanteric pressure injuries, groin, and lower-to-mid abdominal wall fascial defects.

indications: Trochanteric pressure injury coverage
Full-thickness abdominal wall reconstruction with vascularized fascia lata
Groin / perineal coverage
Intraoperative bailout when ALT perforators are absent
contraindications: Prior lateral hip surgery dividing LCFA ascending branch
advantages: Durable vascularized fascia lata for abdominal wall strength
Reliable pedicle anatomy & easy harvest
Can be sensate via T12/LFCN
disadvantages: Distal third skin necrosis if extended within 8 cm of knee

donor_site.closure: Primary if ≤8–10 cm; STSG if wider.

preoperative_planning: Draw ASIS to lateral femoral condyle line
Mark pedicle entry 8–10 cm below ASIS and stop ≥8 cm proximal to knee
technique.design: Anterior border along ASIS–lateral patella line; keep distal margin ≥8 cm above knee.
harvest_steps: 1. Incise distal/lateral margins through fascia lata and elevate subfascially off vastus lateralis.
2. Proceed proximally into plane between TFL and gluteus medius / rectus femoris.
3. Identify ascending LCFA pedicle entering deep surface of TFL ~8–10 cm below ASIS.
4. Rotate posteriorly for trochanteric ulcer or superomedially for groin/abdominal wall.
pearls: Keep distal tip at least 8–10 cm above lateral knee joint to avoid distal random-zone necrosis.
pitfalls: Mistaking distal fascial-only extension for reliable muscular skin perfusion.

references.book: Mathes SJ, Nahai F. Reconstructive Surgery: Principles, Anatomy, & Technique
